newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil coffee auction likely to see good demand.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee auction likely to see good demand.

text.p: Brazilian coffee roasters expect to see good demand at an auction Wednesday of government coffee stocks and have already asked for larger quantities to be made available in next month's sale, an official said.
"There is a shortage of coffee for us to make blends," said David Nahum, secretary-general of the Brazil Coffee Industry Association which represents roasters.

"The crop which has just been picked is still too young for us to use, there is really nothing left in the market from the previous crop and the only people who have coffee from other crops is the government," he added.
The government will at 1400 local/1700 GMT tomorrow put up 30,000 60-kg bags for auction but roasters have already asked that at least 100,000 bags be offered in the next sale on October 23.
"We would like to have had at least 100,000 bags for this auction but the total had already been decided before we made our request," Nahum said.
The government has mapped out an agenda of monthly sales until December and plans further regular auctions through to the end of the coffee year in June 1997.

The quantity offered is not to exceed 200,000 bags per sale but depends on prevailing current supply. Given the current harvest, auctions so far this coffee year have been very small, with 34,824 bags bought out of a total on offer of 35,023 bags.

Roasters should be able to start using the 1996/97 crop for blending from November but auction sizes should increase anyway throughout the coffee year as domestic supply starts to fall off, Nahum said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
